target: Clean F-15C with two F100-PW-220 engines, gear up, no external stores, subsonic; matching weight/CG and measured input are required per test

sources.title: NASA TM-72861: Precision Controllability of the F-15 Airplane
sources.review: Full PDF reviewed. Appendix printed pp. 12–13 documents control architecture and authority; Table 1, pp. 15–16, supplies dimensions and surface limits. Figures 8 and 11 contain tracking time histories, not full-stick roll tests.
sources.reason: Used for pitch CAS ±10°, limiter breakpoints +5°/−19°, yaw CAS ±5°, washed-out pitch-rate feedback, and dimensional checks. Early F-15/PW-100, with control-system changes during testing: not matched F-15C flight-performance validation. Gains, taper shape, washout constants, virtual-stick gearing and combined roll authority remain estimates.

sources.title: NASA TM-104255: Flight Testing and Simulation of an F-15 Airplane Using Throttles for Flight Control
sources.review: Full PDF reviewed, particularly printed pp. 2 and 11–16; Figures 9, 10 and 14 contain measured response histories.
sources.reason: Preproduction F-15A with F100 EMD/PW-1128 engines and deliberately nonproduction low-power response. The illustrated comparison cases use throttles-only emergency control, gear down and emergency inlet positions. They do not validate our clean PW-229 stick response.

sources.title: NASA TM-2003-212027: Real-Time Stability and Control Derivative Extraction From F-15 Flight Data
sources.review: Official abstract reviewed; full PDF could not be retrieved in this environment.
sources.reason: Modified research aircraft; useful identification methodology, but no matched numeric flight trace imported or qualified.

sources.title: Pitch-Axis Aerodynamic Parameter Identification for NASA’s F-15B
sources.review: Official abstract reviewed; NTRS lists no available download.
sources.reason: Canard-equipped F-15B TN 837. Canard coupling and pitch instability do not match the current generic airframe.

sources.title: NASA TM-2012-215978: Flight Test Results on the Stability and Control of the F-15 Quiet Spike Aircraft
sources.review: Official abstract reviewed; full PDF exceeds the web reader’s size limit.
sources.reason: F-15B with telescoping nose boom. Baseline configurations may be useful, but baseline traces and complete test conditions have not been extracted or qualified.
